extraction.name: TravelPlanner
extraction.description: A benchmark for evaluating language agents on real-world travel planning with tool use and multiple constraints, containing a sandbox environment, tools over nearly four million records, and 1,225 curated queries with reference plans.
extraction.creator: Jian Xie; Kai Zhang; Jiangjie Chen; Tinghui Zhu; Renze Lou; Yuandong Tian; Yanghua Xiao; Yu Su
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was constructed by setting up a static closed sandbox environment, designing diverse travel queries from sampled elements and constraints, generating natural language queries with GPT-4, having graduate students annotate feasible reference plans, and performing author review and budget recalibration for quality control.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Web API, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data came from publicly available Internet data, including the Kaggle Flight Status Prediction dataset, Google Distance Matrix API, Kaggle Zomato Restaurants Dataset, Google Places API, and Kaggle Airbnb Open Data Dataset.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: The collected source data was modified by adding, deleting, and altering keys and values; prices and categorical attributes were also generated or randomly assigned for some resources.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For each source, selected fields were extracted and others discarded; search results from APIs were stored in fixed databases to create a static evaluation environment.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Twenty graduate students manually annotated plans for synthesized queries, and a plan was accepted only if it satisfied all constraints in the evaluation script; authors then reviewed every query and plan and corrected errors.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Annotated plans underwent detailed author review, error correction, and budget recalibration based on human-annotated plan costs, with multiple stages of human verification to ensure quality and feasibility.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to support future research on complex planning, and the authors note that commonsense definitions may vary and encourage broader discussion; they also prohibit cheating on validation and test sets to preserve fairness and reliability.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The authors note that commonsense judgments may vary across people, and that their current evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark uses a static and closed sandbox rather than dynamic real-world data, and its commonsense evaluation criteria are based on the authors' consensus.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluating language agents for tool use and complex multi-constraint planning; the dataset is split into training, validation, and test sets, and the authors encourage using evaluation feedback in the training set while prohibiting cheating on validation and test sets.

name.evidence: To advance this investigation, we propose TravelPlanner, a new planning benchmark that focuses on travel planning, a common real-world planning scenario.

description.evidence: We introduce TravelPlanner, a benchmark crafted for evaluating language agents in tool-use and complex planning within multiple constraints.

rai:dataCollection.evidence: This section outlines the construction pipeline of TravelPlanner, which involves the following steps: 1) Environment and evaluation setup. 2) Diverse travel query design. 3) Reference plan annotation. 4) Quality check.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: TravelPlanner provides a rich sandbox environment with around four million data entries crawled from the Internet that can be accessed via six tools. We also meticulously curate 1,225 diverse user queries (along with their reference plans)... To ensure every query has at least one feasible plan, we invite 20 graduate students to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: The original data for each tool is sourced from publicly available Internet data.

rai:dataCollectionTimeframe.evidence: From this dataset, we extract data spanning from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We then modify this data, which includes adding, deleting, and altering certain keys and values to suit our requirements.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: From this dataset, we extract data spanning from 2022-03-01 to 2022-04-01. We specifically included fields like “FlightDate”, “DepTime”, “ArrTime”, “ActualElapsedTime”, “Distance”, “OriginCityName”, and “DestCityName” while discarding other values.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: To ensure every query has at least one feasible plan, we invite 20 graduate students to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries. One plan is deemed eligible only if it meets all the constraints outlined in our evaluation script, which is detailed in Section 3.4.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: To ensure the quality of each natural language query and its corresponding annotated plan, the authors performed a detailed review of every query and plan, rectifying any errors found.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: To ensure every query has at least one feasible plan, we invite 20 graduate students to meticulously annotate plans for synthesized queries.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Finally, based on elements, we utilize GPT-4 (OpenAI, 2023) to generate natural language queries.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: TravelPlanner aims to provide an effective benchmark for complex planning in future research.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: We realize that everyone’s definition of commonsense may be different. Our current evaluation criteria are based on the authors’ consensus, and we encourage additional discussions to enrich our commonsense dimension, aiming for a more thorough evaluation.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: In TravelPlanner, we create a static and closed sandbox environment for consistent and unbiased evaluations.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The dataset is divided into the training, validation, and test set.
